quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: At night, if oncoming headlights are too bright, where should you look?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the road will curve ahead.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase.
Maintain.
Vary.
Reduce.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop. Stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You find a defect that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you can afford it.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is repaired.

questions.question: Night driving is ____ than daytime driving.

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Oncoming headlights can blind you. Tired or impaired drivers are more likely to be on the road at night.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to move out of the way.
Stop and block the emergency vehicle.
Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
Signal when it is clear for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
questions.explanation: Make every effort to give emergency vehicles a clear path. If safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic signal?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing before crossing.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. Change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. Change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, distracted, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey above the others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override traffic signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, highway workers, and school crossing guards are authorized to direct traffic.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is going under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither lane can cross them, except when turning into a driveway or business entrance. No passing is allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When entering heavy traffic on an interstate, what rule applies?

options.text: The entering driver has the right-of-way.
Drivers on the interstate must wave the entering driver in.
The entering driver must yield to drivers already on the interstate.
You do not need to use a signal when merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entering driver must yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: Drivers entering the interstate must yield to vehicles already on it. Always use your signal when merging.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two-way traffic is coming.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, what must you allow for?

options.text: The longer stopping distance large vehicles need.
The shorter stopping distance large vehicles need.
The quieter noise from large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance large vehicles need.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in a position where the truck driver can see you and where the truck does not block your view of the road.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means you cannot do something. These signs are white with red and black markings and tell you what actions are not allowed.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is going. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What is a good passing rule?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Every pass increases the chance of a collision. If you drive faster than others, you will need to keep passing. Drive at the legal speed with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
